messages.text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

For me, it matters that we can make coffee reliably without this becoming a conflict; I’m tired and can’t take on chasing everyone or handling the repair. The grinder and shared use matter because we all use them daily, but I don’t know what should happen with them. I don’t want to take sides on the sisters’ disagreement. Nothing else feels off to me right now.

#2 is broadly right: I’d lean toward a simpler machine that needs little upkeep. I’m worn out after long days, and what matters is having some freedom from ongoing repairs, cleaning, or a long discussion about it—I can’t take those on. I know the old machine matters to B, so I don’t want to dismiss that. The list seems okay, though #5 should be checked with me in my own words.

#3 is my concern: I want the old machine repaired and kept. It was our dad’s, and letting it go feels like losing a piece of him—but the repeated breakdowns are wearing me down, and I have little time to chase repairs. I need this not to keep draining me. I use the grinder daily too, but I’m not sure what should happen with it separately. No issue with the list or process.
The wording fits for #1, #4, #6, #7 and #8. #5 fits too; I’d keep clear that I can’t take on chasing or repairs. I don’t have another concern with the list or process right now.
No further discomfort from me right now. I’m not ready to add anything else.

#5 fits: I need this to stay manageable, especially since I can’t take on repairs, cleaning, or a long discussion. B’s connection to Dad’s machine matters to me because I want to respect what matters to her. The grinder’s daily use should be considered too, though I’m not sure what should happen with it. The list is okay; I do feel some discomfort about this turning into a long back-and-forth.

#3 fits better as “respect for what this machine means to me.” #12, #14 and #15 fit. #13 and #5 fit too: I have little time to chase repairs, and I don’t want this to keep draining me. I understand A wants less upkeep because she’s worn out; I just don’t want that to mean the machine’s history gets dismissed. No discomfort with the process, as long as it stays manageable.
I meant I have no more concerns to add, not that I’m holding back. I don’t think #16 needs an NCE.

Those candidates fit broadly: easy, dependable coffee; freedom from upkeep and a manageable effort; and respect for what matters to B. The grinder matters because we all use it daily, though I’m unsure whether it should be decided on separately. I’m still uncomfortable with the amount of back-and-forth, so I’d like to pause here for now.
#3 and #20 fit: I want respect for what this machine means to me. #21 fits too, as long as the process stays brief and doesn’t become another thing I have to manage. No other discomfort.
Yes, I’m a little uncomfortable with the repeated follow-ups. I’d appreciate leaving this paused for now.
Nothing’s off in my items, and I’m not holding back. But all this repeated checking is getting cumbersome; keep it brief. I don’t want to answer for A while she’s paused.
#24 fits. #25 fits; don’t answer for A while she’s paused. Keep this brief.
The repeated long lists and check-ins are getting cumbersome. Please don’t ask me to reconfirm settled items; my needs are as stated, and I have no new concern.
